=== FILE: Can Taking Vitamin D Help Lower Blood Sugar？ #docgerrytan #endocrinologist #bloodpressure [VDwbOcDYDPQ].en.txt ===

Can vitamin D supplementation help control your glucose? I'm Dr. Jerry Tan, I'm a Mayo Clinic trained endocrinologist. Evidence from epidemiological studies suggest that vitamin D deficiency is associated with reduced insulin release and development of type 2 diabetes. In this study led by Wei Chen, they analyzed 39 randomized controlled trials involving 3,000 participants to see if vitamin D actually helps manage blood sugar. They found that vitamin D group compared to placebo group significantly reduced A1c by 0.3% fasting blood glucose reduced by 0.49 millimoles per liter with improvement in insulin resistance. Furthermore, the meta-analysis revealed that vitamin D is most effective as a complementary treatment when the following conditions are met. First, those started with low vitamin D levels showed the biggest improvement. Those high-dose short-term supplementation was more effective than low doses over a very long period of time. And the effects were more prominent in patients who were overweight. Including those starting with an A1c of 8% or higher showed more significant progress. The study also found that a dose as high as 2,000 international units per day provided a marked improvement in glycemic control and fasting blood sugar as long as the duration of supplementation was over 12 weeks. Again, for more health tips, please follow me in my YouTube channel Dr. Jerry Tan. See you around.

=== FILE: Finger Workout That Can Help Lower Blood Pressure #docgerrytan #endocrinologist #highbp [cXEu6f9u8zs].en.txt ===

Let me share you another finger maneuver to help lower your blood pressure. I'm Dr. Jerry Tan Mayo Clinic trained endocrinologist. In this study of hypertensive elderly individuals, they evaluated the effect of this finger therapy on blood pressure. The intervention involved a fingertip maneuver where they place fingertips of both hands together, not the palms, then push fingertips gently together, keeping the palms apart. Now they then hold this position for 15 seconds, then relax for 10 seconds. Now the process is repeated five to 10 times. The study clearly showed a significant reduction in blood pressure where the systolic blood pressure dropped from 152 mm mercury to post intervention blood pressure of 142. Likewise, the diastolic blood pressure dropped from 97 mm mercury to a postintervention blood pressure of 92 with a mean drop of 5 mm mercury. While this drop might seem modest, it is statistically significant and demonstrates that this relaxation technique can be an effective non-farmacological supplement to help manage hypertension. Furthermore, it's a simple maneuver that you can do anytime at any day to help lower your blood pressure. Again, for more health tips, please follow me in my YouTube channel, Doc Cherry Tan. Review how to approach COVID-19 cases in terms of proper isolation and quarantine. Now once a person is positive for COVID-19, then that person definitely should isolate with the purpose of preventing COVID-19 virus from spreading to other contacts. Getting isolated therefore is an obligation. Likewise, it is one's responsibility to follow to protect your loved ones and friends from getting COVID-19. So if you got COVID-19 but asymptomatic, then you tested antigen positive, but you are fully vaccinated, then please do isolate yourself. Don't go out and expose others for at least seven days from the time you got your positive result. If, however, you develop symptoms on the third or the fourth day or any time during the isolation period, then start again as day one on the first day you develop your symptoms. If, however, you got COVID-19 positive test, you're still asymptomatic, but you are unvaccinated, then please isolate longer, and this time for at least 10 days from the positive result. Now, if you got COVID-19 positive test, this time you are symptomatic, but only mild with fever and cough, but you are fully vaccinated, then isolate for at least seven days from the start of symptoms. You can safely stop your isolation on the 10th day as long as, again, you're afebrile without fever for the past 24 hours, and literally your symptoms are improving. Now, the isolation procedures change if you are elderly with mild symptoms, but with comorbidities like diabetes, then here is the difference. Regardless of your vaccination status, please isolate for at least 10 days from the start of symptoms. You can only safely stop your isolation on the 10th day as long as, again, you have no fever for the past 24 hours, and your symptoms are improving. Now, if, however, you develop severe or critical case of COVID-19, again, regardless of the vaccination status, isolation should at least be 21 days from the start of symptoms, and that patient can safely stop isolation on the 21st day as long as that patient has been afebrile for 24 hours or the symptoms are improving. Now, if any time during the isolation period, you try testing for COVID-19 antigen and you tested negative, remind you that the test, even if it's negative, cannot in any way shorten the minimum required isolation days. Now, your siblings or your friends who have been exposed to you being COVID-19, if he or she is asymptomatic and fully vaccinated, then that exposed individual or friend do not need to quarantine himself, but he is required to do intensive self-monitoring for the next 14 days, and during that period to always wear a mask, even at home, especially if he is living with somebody who is categorized at high risk. If at any time the one exposed within the 14-day period develops symptoms, then he needs to start isolation counting at day one of the symptom occurrence, regardless of the testing results. If, however, if the one exposed is unvaccinated or partially vaccinated, then they need to quarantine longer for at least 14 days, since this is the long incubation period of COVID-19. If at any time during the quarantine period, he develops symptoms, then he needs to start isolation back to day one on the time of his symptoms, regardless of the testing results. Now, we all know that inflammatory arthritis come in second, and that includes rheumatoid arthritis or gouty arthritis. Now, what then are some of the dietary interventions that can potentially help reduce symptom severity among my patients or people with joint pains to hopefully improve their overall quality of life? That's what's this. Let me share you some foods and beverages that I usually ask my patients to avoid if they do complain of some joint pains. So with my predominant patient population, which is with diabetes, of course, the number one of the list to avoid is added sugar. Now, added sugars usually include sugars coming from candies, ice cream, soda, sweetened beverages like milk tea, including juices, as studies have shown that they can really worsen joint pains. Furthermore, sugary beverages like soda actually can significantly increase your risk of arthritis, such that studies have shown that drinking fructose, sweetened beverages five times per week were three times more likely to have arthritis as a symptom than those patients who only consume few to no fructose, sweetened beverages. As with my previous blogs, foods you eat should, in general, be part of a healthy meal plan for whatever conditions you're trying to avoid. But there are also certain foods that are in common to most of these chronic conditions that we should avoid. And one of them would be red meat. Red meats, as we know, are common foods that we always advocate to avoid, as in general, they're not really truly a healthy food. Now, some research have also linked that red meats has been shown to be associated with inflammation. And we all know that inflammation may increase arthritis symptoms. Furthermore, studies have shown that a high red meat intake can be an important risk factor for you to develop inflammatory arthritis. Conversely, if you do plant-based diets that exclude red meat, they have been shown to improve arthritis symptoms. Third on the list would be highly processed foods. Now, these are due to demands of our times and busy schedules. Most of us have resorted to ultra-processed foods for easier access during mealtime, especially breakfast. So these ultra-processed foods include breakfast cereals and baked goods. And we all know that there are plenty in the Philippines. But they are, remember, typically high in refined grains, added sugar, preservatives, and other potentially inflammatory ingredients that have been shown to worsen joint pains. The fourth on the list would be alcohol. Now, especially if the joint pains is due to high uric acid. We all know that alcohol should be avoided as studies have shown that alcohol intake may increase the frequency and severity of gouty arthritis by increasing your uric acid. Likewise, as alcohol in general may worsen arthritis symptoms, anyone, therefore, with inflammatory arthritis should restrict or avoid it. Moreover, we have new data to support that chronic alcohol consumption is also associated with increased risk of osteoarthritis. Therefore, if you start having symptoms of joint pains, refrain from alcohol. If on the list would be certain vegetable oils, what we know is that diets rich in omega-6 fatty acids and low in omega-3 may worsen symptoms of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. So diets high in omega-3 fatty acids include diets that contain fatty fish like salmon. So the two servings of fish per week should provide you with enough omega-3 fatty acid for health. It is more of the imbalance between omega-3 and omega-6 that we see in most western diets that have been shown to increase arthritis symptoms. Bottom line is, it is best to reduce your intake of foods high in omega-6, such as vegetable oils, while increasing your intake of omega-3 foods, like fatty fish, to improve arthritis symptoms. Six on the list would be high salt foods. Now, this includes any canned goods. You usually like canned goods for breakfast, canned soup, pizza, certain cheeses or processed meats like bacon, tocino, or luncheon meat. Now, studies have shown that arthritis symptoms do get worse when fed on a high salt diet than those on a diet containing normal salt levels. And those fed with low salt diet had also less cartilage breakdown and bone destruction, as well as lower inflammatory markers, suggesting benefit to arthritic changes. Lastly, is to avoid foods with high advanced glycation end products. So what are these? Advanced glycation end products are the molecules that naturally exist in uncooked animal foods that are formed through certain cooking methods created through interactions between sugar, protein, and fats. Now, high protein, high fat animal foods that are fried, roasted, grilled, seared, or broiled are among the richest in dietary sources of advanced glycation end products. Examples include bacon, pan-fried or grilled steak, roasted or fried chicken, or broiled hot dogs. They are culprits for high AGEs that may increase the risk of arthritic symptoms. Of course, there are other foods that are also high in AGEs and they include French fries, American cheeses, margarine, and mayonnaise. We therefore advise patients to try replacing high AGE foods with nutritious whole foods like vegetables, fruits, legumes, and fish to hopefully reduce the total advanced glycation end products in your body. So the bottom line of my talk today is that just like any other diseases like diabetes or high blood pressure or high cholesterol, if you happen to have arthritis, a healthy diet and a lifestyle may help improve your symptoms. Make sure also you exercise. Lastly, to help alleviate your risk of developing arthritis, it is also best to always include lifestyle factors like your activity level, body weight, and smoking status, as they are also vital in managing arthritis. Again, this is Dr. Jerry Tan. Stay safe. See you again soon.

First, we have to remember that bread is low in essential nutrients. For breakfast or for snacks, bread, if compared to other foods like fruits and vegetables, it is relatively, without question, very low in essential nutrients like protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals. And therefore, most breads contain gluten. So for those who need gluten-free food, bread should be one of those that you should stay away. Though most people digest gluten easily, the problem with some is that they cannot tolerate it, or some people may have sensitivity to gluten and therefore allergic reaction to it, which can result in issues like stomach pain or bloating. Now, for these individuals, the best option would be gluten-free breads, typically made from tapioca, brown rice, or potato flours instead of wheat flour, which actually can be tolerated better or well among these patients who are gluten sensitive. In short, bread almost always contains gluten, which can cause some adverse side effects for people with increased sensitivity to gluten, resulting in uncomfortable abdominal symptoms. So when you eat bread, what happens is that your body breaks it down to glucose, leading to an increase in blood sugar levels. We know that increase in blood sugar levels triggers the pancreas to produce insulin. insulin is an anabolic hormone and therefore drives calories inside the fat cell. As long as insulin levels is high, then the fat cell cannot break it down or cannot release glucose, and therefore the rest of the body will be deprived of glucose. This will then make you crave for more sweets. So understandably, therefore, more sugar leads to more hunger because of high insulin, and therefore leads to increased body weight. So if you really like to eat bread, do it on occasions. Then I would advise that you opt for certain varieties such as the whole grain bread, which are high in fiber, which can slow the absorption of sugar in your bloodstream and hopefully help stabilize your blood sugar without necessarily increasing glucose levels in blood. In short, bread's high carbohydrate content is a no-no. It can increase blood sugar and hunger while possibly promoting a higher body weight and increased risk of diabetes diabetes and metabolic syndrome. So how do I advise my patients? Now, the most common probiotic that you may be taking already, which you didn't know, that is also readily available, is the lactobacillus. And therefore, if you see a product with no approved therapeutic claim, it means you take them at your own risk. So in general, probiotic foods and supplements, however, are safe for most people, although some people I caution with immune system problems or other serious health conditions should not take them. In this review, caffeine consumption was shown to reduce total sleep by 45 minutes and sleep efficiency by 7% with an increase in sleep onset latency of 9 minutes and wake after sleep onset of 12 minutes. Caffeine works by blocking adinosine, a chemical that builds up in your brain throughout the day to make you feel sleepy.  And then normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal normal as an endocrinologist where 80 to 90 percent of my diabetic population are either overweight or obese and this has been a very common question. Can I try apple cider vinegar because they have been shown to help in weight loss? Can apple cider vinegar help patients lose weight? Let's watch this. We know that apple cider vinegar is actually made in a two-step fermentation process. Once the apples are crushed, they're combined with yeast and then once converted into sugar, into alcohol and the bacteria is added, this will then ferment the alcohol into acetic acid. Yes, it's an acid because acetic acid, which is the main active component of the apple cider vinegar, constitutes around five to six percent made up of acetic acid, which is responsible for the main effect of satiety. So calorie-wise, one tablespoon of apple cider vinegar only contains approximately three calories and zero carbs. So claims of apple cider and its weight loss effect actually mainly comes from some animal studies that suggest that acetic acid in apple cider vinegar may promote weight loss in several ways, which have been shown to favor fat burning. In fact, studies like this have shown that when rats were exposed to acetic acid, it increased an enzyme called AMPK, which clinically or biochemically has been shown to boost fat burning and decreases fat and sugar production in the liver. So furthermore, one other study supporting the claim that acetate or the acetic acid may suppress centers in your brain that control appetite, which can therefore lead to food intake reduction. So although the results of the animal studies look promising, let me caution you that we need to confirm research specifically human studies to confirm these findings. Now apple cider vinegar has been shown to promote fullness, which therefore can lead to a reduction in caloric intake. The mechanism for which why patients eat fewer calories with apple cider remains to be known. But at present, in addition to its appetite suppressing effects, it has been shown to also slow the rate at which food cleaves the stomach. So this effect therefore makes the patient feel fuller, faster, and therefore can help lower glucose and insulin levels. Now we have very few human studies looking at apple cider vinegar, and weight loss. And in one human study, it showed some impressive effects on weight and body fat. In this 12-week study of 144 obese Japanese adults who consumed either one tablespoon of vinegar, or two tablespoons of the vinegar, or placebo. Placebo means it does not really contain vinegar, and they drank it every day. These individuals were told to restrict their alcohol intake, but otherwise to continue their usual diet and activity throughout the study. And the results showed significant benefit. Those patients who were on one to two tablespoons of vinegar per day had weight loss of around 2.6 to 3.7 pounds of weight loss. There was approximately 0.7 to 0.9 percent reduction in body fat percentage, a reduction in the weight circumference by 0.5 to 0.7 percent, and biochemically, a reduction of approximately 26 percent in triglycerides. Concluding that based on this small study, adding one to two tablespoons of apple cider vinegar to your diet may help you lose weight, reduce body fat percentage, make you lose belly fat, and decrease your blood triglycerides. However, this is only one of the very few human studies, fairly large, wherein the results are encouraging, but I caution you, additional studies are needed. So if you opt to use apple cider vinegar based on these few studies, here's how to add it to your diet. An easy method is to use it with olive oil for salad dressing. It can also be used for pickling vegetables, or you can simply mix it with water and drink it. Now, the amount of apple cider vinegar for weight loss is one to two tablespoons per day mixed with water. It is best that you spread this out to two to three doses throughout the day, and it may be best to drink it before meals. Taking more than what is recommended can also have potentially harmful effects, as drug interactions can occur, or erosion of the tooth enamel can happen. It is also best to start off with one teaspoon per day to see how you tolerate it. Remember, do not take more than one tablespoon at a time, because taking too much at one sitting may actually cause nausea, and undiluted vinegar may actually burn inside your mouth or esophagus. So the bottom line is, at the end of the day, taking moderate amounts of apple cider vinegar appears in few studies to promote weight loss and provide a number of other health benefits. Although we believe that other vinegars, other types of vinegars may actually provide similar benefits, but these vinegars with lower acetic acid content, but also have less potent benefits. So scientific studies on apple cider vinegar's ability to help with weight loss, again, continues to be limited. It is very important that everyone remembers or realizes that there is no magic bullet for weight loss. Now, I'm not saying that if you're going to take this apple cider vinegar, you're going to get significant weight loss. Now, while studies have shown that there was pretty significant weight loss, the meager results of weight loss with this apple cider vinegar, data pale in comparison to other popular diets, exercise, and weight loss programs. So anecdotally, some patients report that including a tablespoon of diluted apple cider vinegar in the diet do make them feel fuller and therefore makes them less eat, less appetite, and better satiety, and therefore results in reduced snack cravings between dinner and bedtime. So perhaps apple cider vinegar do help with weight loss, perhaps simply because of appetite suppression. But until we have more solid research, the jury is still out. What we know at the present time as an endocrinologist, I continue to advocate a nutritious diet with daily exercise to remain as the cornerstone of a scientifically proven weight loss program. It certainly is not as easy as just mixing apple cider vinegar with water or popping a pill, but the rewards start immediately and pay dividends for your health for the years to come. And remember, always remember, for health, for weight, there is no magic pill for healthy weight loss. Be skeptical of any claim otherwise. Again, this is Dr. Jerry Tan. See you again soon.

 nassiongroom, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, nassionante, with COVID-19 infection, we are now slowly gathering more data about the so-called risk of those infected with COVID-19 with regard to long COVID syndrome, specifically for those who have been infected for the last two years. The question is, if any of you were infected with COVID-19, are you at risk of COVID-19, long COVID syndrome? That's what's this. We know that getting sick from COVID-19 is not fun. Long COVID, which is often defined as constellation of symptoms experienced for 12 weeks or more after a COVID diagnosis, is actually a medley of bad symptoms that can occur and affect us for months. Range of symptoms from fatigue to breathlessness to problems related to the brain, such as lack of mental clarity, estimated to have affected more than 10 to 100 million people worldwide. Now, the intriguing news is that now data have come up and have shown that the symptoms do affect us even several years after COVID-19 infection, and that after the so-called full recovery from COVID-19 infection. Now, in this recent publication in Lancet, the study found that those adults exposed to COVID-19 or infected with COVID-19 were at risk of developing the following seizure disorders, brain fog, dementia, and other mental health conditions up to two years after recovering from COVID-19. On the other hand, children who were infected with COVID-19 had a higher chance of being diagnosed with epilepsy or seizures, encephalitis, and nerve root disorders. Now, there was also a small but worrisome risk of being diagnosed with a psychotic disorder, such as schizophrenia or delusional thinking. Now, the study, however, could not exactly tell if the people had experienced ongoing symptoms for the full two years since the COVID-19 diagnosis was made. The reason for that is the study only looked at the number of new diagnoses being made, not the persistence of the duration of symptoms. Now, for adults, however, the data was clear that the risk of developing brain fog, dementia, psychotic disorders, epilepsy, and seizures remain elevated throughout the two years. Now, for the elderly, on the other hand, over the age of 65, once they have exposed and infected with COVID-19, these individuals had a 1.2% increase in risk of being diagnosed with dementia. Now, on the other hand, the risk of brain fog in children was noted to be transient, meaning there was no overall increased risk at any greater risk of being diagnosed with anxiety or depression after COVID-19, even in the first six months. But what I don't like or what I consider as worst news is that children who have been infected with COVID-19 had a twofold increased risk of epilepsy and seizures and a threefold increased risk of a psychotic disorder diagnosis in two years after having COVID. Now, what then is the long-term impact of this finding overall? Now, the evidence is particularly worrisome because even as the new COVID-19 variants are considered to be milder, we believe they still appear to have the same long-term consequences. For now, it seems that what we really know is much less than what we think we know about long COVID. It is therefore our appeal that we all remain vigilant not to let our guard down. === FILE: Why eating dinner early is better for your health #docgerrytan #endocrinologist [Ms5n-J6NWOI].en.txt ===

Here's another reason why you should have early dinner. I am Dr. Jerry Tan Mayo Clinic trained in endocrinologist. Early dinner or more than 12-hour fasting between dinner and breakfast has many advantages such as weight loss, lower risk of diabetes, including cancer and death. Whereas late dinner is not a healthy habit. In fact, in a recent randomized crossover trial, they found that eating dinner at 6 versus 900 p.m. of same calorie meal led to lower mean 24-hour blood glucose levels, and improved substrate oxidation, fat versus carbohydrate burning the next morning. The study showed that late dinner eaters had peaked blood glucose levels almost 20% higher, and fat burning reduced by 10% compared to early eaters. Most likely because with early dinners, there tends to be less late night snacking, possibly fewer total calories consumed, better appetite regulation, and possibly increase fat oxidation. Likewise, early dinner can be part of your protocol of intermittent fasting with your first meal around noon. Tips to adopt an early dinner habit is trying to finish your main evening meal 2 to three hours or more before bedtime so digestion is underway before you lie down. And always aim for consistent dinner time daily. Again, for more health tips, please follow me in my YouTube channel, Doc Jan.
